subject.name: Fraud Examiners, Investigators and Analysts
subject.summary: Occupational definition | O*NET-SOC13-2099.04 involves obtaining evidence and statements concerning fraud allegations, preparing reports and testifying about findings, and may include coordinating detection and prevention activities. The 23 tasks include documenting investigations, maintaining record databases, examining financial documents, bills and business relationships, interviewing, assessing whether further investigation is needed, recommending action, participating in or leading teams, coordinating with attorneys and law enforcement, preparing court evidence and testifying, developing and maintaining detection tools and procedures, conducting in-depth investigations such as money laundering inquiries, training and tracking trends, assessing business risks, researching new technology, observing in the field, obtaining and serving subpoenas, arresting persons intended to be charged with fraud, and negotiating recovery of losses. The official list includes the last three tasks; they cannot be excluded across the board. Jurisdiction, procedures and job authority require separate verification; a job title or task list does not itself grant these powers.
